persons.name: William Catton
persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Catton, William' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 1 July 1835, column 4 — dated 1835-07-01. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). persons.name: Dr William Bradshaw Egan
persons.note: BORN NEAR LAKE KILLARNEY, COUNTY KERRY, IRELAND, 28 SEPTEMBER 1808 - the best-documented foreign origin in the parcel. Andreas: 'In the fall of 1833 Dr. William Bradshaw Egan came to the city.' He was appointed to the health committee for the South Division on 22 August 1834 and delivered the oration when ground was broken for the Illinois & Michigan Canal on 4 July 1836. He bought the Tremont House block from General Beaubien and built five houses on it, known as Egan's Row - which is why a physician is also one of the town's builders. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 2 times: Tax list of the Town of Chicago, 1833 — “Egan, William Bradshaw” (tax_1833_028, line 80); Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Egan, William Bradshaw” (poll_1834_038, line 207). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Egan' agrees with the entry's forenames; 2 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json). FERGUS 1839'S LATER LISTS — 1837 AND 1839 EVIDENCE, NEVER AN 1835 FACT. Fergus' Chicago Directory for 1839 names this person 1 time in its two later lists: the poll of Chicago's first city election, 2 May 1837 — “William B. Egan” (f1839_v0600, printed page 45, ward 6, voting for William B. Ogden). What a match may carry, and it is short: that the man was in Chicago on 2 May 1837 and in that ward. It is written as 1837 evidence with describes_date 1837-05-02, never as an 1835 fact, and the person's grade does not move on this alone. Under the ratified ladder a second contemporary source is what lifts projected_resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE, not about July 1835. The ward is a location in the CITY of 1837, whose six wards are drawn on printed page 46; it is not a location in the town of 1835 and does not place a house. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: Surname 'Egan' folds to the same string as the 1837 entry's, and the given name of both begins W. (data/research/directories/fergus_1839_election_crosswalk_1835.json and fergus_1839_register_crosswalk_1835.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date — or a register four years after it — is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE rather than about July 1835. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict. THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 43 times, as “EGAN WILLIAM B”, “EGAN W B”, “EGAN WILLIAM”, 1835-09-03 to 1836-06-26: 6 federal land entries — E2NE sec 20 T38N R14E; THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $66310.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. residents.research_note: AN IRISH DOCTOR WHO ARRIVED FOURTEEN MONTHS BEFORE THE HARBOUR MADE THE TOWN, and the record in this parcel that best answers K1's 'why they came' by refusing to answer it. Every stage of his journey from Kerry is documented; the motive for the last leg is not, and what stands in for it is a biographer's admiring sentence from 1884. THE GAP THIS HOUSEHOLD EXPOSES: eight physicians are documented in the 1833 town and this dataset contains no doctor's office, no apothecary's back room and no hospital outside the fort. That is a structures gap the residents layer has just made visible, which is what it is for.
